entries.title: Court lets Puerto Rico governor fire firm that runs the island's troubled power grid
entries.snippet: LUMA Energy took over the electric grid five years ago. The court's ruling nullifies its contract, and gives the government a year to find a new operator.

entries.snippet: Taylor revealed his battle with Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer in 2022. He was the guitarist of the 1980s English band Duran Duran, whose pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf" and "Rio".

entries.snippet: Americans are expected to spend more than $1 trillion on holiday shopping this year despite concerns about rising prices. PBS News digital video producer Cecilia Lallmann looks at the ways we could shop smarter this year, including with the help of artificial intelligence.

entries.snippet: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons, days after ignoring U.S. President Donald Trump's offer to meet during his recent visit to Asia.

entries.title: Mexico's most powerful cartels adapt as arrests and leadership battles reshape their ranks
entries.snippet: The arrest of another Mexican drug lord over the weekend added to a string of actions against cartels as Mexico intensifies its crackdown on organized crime under mounting pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump and with U.S. intelligence support.

entries.title: What are king tides? These exceptionally high tides are increasingly flooding coastal communities
entries.snippet: King tides are the highest tides of the year, and they are increasingly flooding coastal communities as sea levels rise.

entries.snippet: The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-lofty goal of Elon Musk's rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists.

entries.title: Trump calls GDP figures 'fake' and demands an investigation of Commerce Department
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump on Thursday accused his Commerce Department of purposely issuing incorrect economic growth figures before the midterm elections, and said he wants to launch an investigation.

entries.title: Judge blocks FCC from early license review for ABC, which network says has had a chilling effect
entries.snippet: A federal judge on Wednesday blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses, agreeing with the network that the Trump administration was chilling the network's free speech rights.

entries.title: King tides and strong waves destroy part of Pacifica pier as officials warn of coastal flooding
entries.snippet: King tides combined with powerful waves destroyed part of a pier in Northern California on Wednesday, and officials warned more beachfront homes are at risk of flooding.

entries.title: Albania's youth are protesting in Flamingo Revolution, not leaving the country anymore
entries.snippet: Youth protests against a rigid political system and corruption have shaken the government of Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama. They also show that fewer young people are willing to emigrate in search of a better future.

entries.title: Gerard Depardieu to stand trial in France for rape and sexual assault
entries.snippet: The Paris Court of Appeal upheld the order for the 77-year-old French actor to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting an actress in 2018.

entries.title: Guinea-Bissau junta delays presidential vote for 2 years
entries.snippet: The decision came exactly one year after the military took power on November 26, 2025. The junta said the conditions were insufficient to hold presidential elections for now.

entries.title: Trial of Berlin woman accused of spying for Russia begins after delay
entries.snippet: Despite delays due to health issues, the trial of the Berlin woman accused of spying for Russia has begun. Prosecutors say the defendant used her military contacts to provide information on German defense and Ukraine.

entries.title: Saudi pop music is thriving — but for the right reasons?
entries.snippet: As part of Vision 2030, Saudi Arabia's music scene has evolved hugely thanks to state funding and support. Local musicians and DJs are optimistic. But are they actually just helping prop up an authoritarian state?

entries.title: On farewell trip, Steinmeier calls for more investment in Africa
entries.snippet: Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, Kenya: On his last trip to Africa, outgoing German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier called on companies at home to be bolder and seize opportunities in Africa.

entries.title: Trump says he urged Putin to 'pull back' military aggression in Europe
entries.snippet: US President Donald Trump claimed that he talked with Vladimir Putin about ceasing Russia's military aggression in Europe and expressed his belief in the possibility of a deal between Russia and Ukraine.

entries.title: Protests in Iraqi Kurdistan at plans for government in Baghdad to take over oil, border crossings
entries.snippet: Thousands have gathered in the capital of northern Iraq's semiautonomous Kurdish region, waving flags and voicing opposition to plans for the federal government to take control of oil operations and border crossings.

entries.title: Germany: IG Metall union says deal reached with employers
entries.snippet: IG Metall, representing millions of workers in Germany's metal and electrical industry, is the country's largest trade union. The deal came after more than 24 hours of talks with employers.

entries.title: Is authoritarian Vietnam ready to phase out the death penalty?
entries.snippet: Vietnam has voted to abolish the death penalty for six more crimes, continuing a decades-long trend of restricting capital punishment.

entries.title: Iranian drone kills 2 Italian workers in Kuwait, Meloni says
entries.snippet: The Italians were employed as technicians for the Italian branch of German arms manufacturer Rheinmetall. One Kuwaiti and one Pakistani national were also injured in the attack. Iran has denied involvement.

entries.title: Africa's opposition voices face growing pressure
entries.snippet: Opposition politicians and government critics say arrests, prosecutions and restrictions on public activity are making it harder to challenge those in power. Is a broader pattern emerging?

entries.title: Freigang banned — Germany star to miss 2027 World Cup
entries.snippet: Germany forward Laura Freigang has been suspended until October 2027 after missing three doping tests, ruling her out of next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil. Freigang has denied any intention to evade controls.

entries.title: FIFA says a cyberattack against it targeted a 'limited set of personal and business information'
entries.snippet: World football's governing body says the cyberattack targeted personal and business information. They struck at a sensitive time for the under-fire organization and its president, Gianni Infantino.

entries.title: EU-Indonesia trade deal opens new markets, but challenges remain
entries.snippet: The agreement offers new export and investment opportunities for Jakarta and Brussels. But can Indonesia turn Europe's growing interest in its markets and critical minerals into sustainable gains at home?

entries.title: Joshua Kimmich critcizes Bayern bosses over Musiala health comments
entries.snippet: Joshua Kimmich has slammed Bayern Munich's leadership over comments about Jamal Musiala's health issues. The bosses have questioned whether the player can return to previous form – and is still worth his high salary.

entries.title: Crew member dies after diesel tanker sinks off Ibiza coast
entries.snippet: Authorities rescued 17 crew members but one later died in hospital after a diesel tanker capsized off the Spanish island of Ibiza. A contingency plan against possible pollution damage is now in place.

entries.title: What is the US permitting bill and would it actually help the climate?
entries.snippet: Sweeping US legislation to speed up energy projects has found rare bipartisan support. Supporters say it would unlock clean energy and lower energy bills, but critics say it's a gift to fossil fuels.

entries.title: Germany news: Cologne court awards record damages in Catholic sex abuse case
entries.snippet: A court has awarded the highest damages ever in Germany to a victim of sexual abuse linked with the Catholic Church. An alleged spy and suspected terrorists are also making headlines in Germany on Thursday. DW has more.
